interventions.speaker: CHAIR

interventions.body: Postoperative prognosis depends on the preoperative PSA and the prostatectomy findings. Extraprostatic extension is documented. Positive surgical margins is reported absent. Seminal vesicle invasion is reported absent. Lymphovascular invasion is reported absent. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are needed to refine this prognosis; a future recurrence date cannot be established from surgical risk factors alone. The fixed estimated horizon is 87.17 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 69.73–104.60 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text: The postoperative pathology indicates a Gleason 4+5 with ISUP grade group 5, pathological stage pT3a. Favorable findings include negative surgical margins, no invasion of the seminal vesicles, absence of lymphovascular invasion, and no lymph node metastasis, as documented by the surgical pathology report: "The robot-assisted radical prostatectomy specimen showed Gleason 4+5 with tertiary pattern 3 (ISUP grade group 5), pathological stage pT3a. Extraprostatic extension was present; surgical margins were negative; the seminal vesicles were not invaded; lymphovascular invasion was absent; there was no lymph node metastasis." The biopsy findings showed Gleason 0+0. Countervailing factors are the preoperative PSA level and the extent of the disease, specifically the presence of extraprostatic extension. Missing postoperative PSA data prevents assessment of biochemical recurrence. The status of nodal sampling is not explicitly detailed, which widens uncertainty regarding regional disease control. Postoperative PSA and its trajectory are crucial information that would revise the prognosis.

nodal_contradiction: The status of nodal sampling is not explicitly detailed, which widens uncertainty regarding regional disease control

attempts.text: The postoperative pathology indicates a Gleason 4+5 with tertiary pattern 3 (ISUP grade group 5) and pathological stage pT3a. Favorable findings include negative surgical margins, as the report states, "surgical margins were negative"; the seminal vesicles were not invaded, and lymphovascular invasion was absent. There was no lymph node metastasis documented. Conversely, the status of nodal sampling is not explicitly detailed, which widens uncertainty regarding regional disease control. The preoperative biopsy showed a Gleason 0+0 (ISUP grade group 0). Postoperative PSA is not recorded, so biochemical recurrence cannot be assessed. The documented negative margins and absence of lymph node metastasis are reassuring findings against the higher preoperative grade. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory is necessary to fully assess the prognosis.
